reviewed_claims.review: The half-modulus exponent (n-1-2i)/2 plus the common untwist (n-1)/2 is exactly n-1-i. Thus arbitrary algebraic automorphisms fix every norm factor, preserve the ordered singleton relation, transport the unique quotient and leave the prescribed inertia fixed. No continuity of the complex field automorphism or invariance of a chosen square root is assumed.

All matrix entries lie in a finite extension of the original K because C is algebraic over the specified embedded K. The sum over the finite quotient is a stable full lattice. It is finite torsion-free, hence free, over both the extension DVR and original DVR after restriction of scalars. Scalar extension splits over all K embeddings; each extends to an automorphism of the algebraic closure, and ITA7 ensures every summand detects exactly the same condition. No extension of the output coefficient ring and no division by the finite group order in O is used.

With column conventions, tau(k)=R(k^-1)^T gives sum_b tau(k)_ab rho(k)F_b = rho(k) f(R(k^-1)e_a). The printed invariant-column equation is therefore exactly fR(k)=rho(k)f. The action is a homomorphism, integral and has the same open kernel. Nonzero families and nonzero intertwiners coincide.

The literal IsoSum hypothesis says the whole module is generated by simple images. The maximal direct-sum argument and complement argument prove semisimplicity and inherited isotypy for all submodules, including infinite-dimensional modules. Finite-dimensional source maps and coordinate projections give the displayed nonvanishing equivalence without a scalar-endomorphism or admissibility assumption.

Each successive Hom functor is a submodule of a finite direct sum for every unprocessed group; commuting product factors preserve the other isotypies. Conditional on nonzero input, ITA10 and ITA8 give exactly the next local condition; zero input remains zero. Finite tensor-Hom adjunction gives the original product invariants and ITA9 gives the same dual column equation. The empty type-place set is included.

scope: Independent mathematical review of ITA7-ITA11 and their literal original IsoSum/product/column contract, with the preceding type and correspondence statements explicitly retained.
limitations: The published crystalline-type scope and the universal IsRecT dictionary are inputs to these five claims; their independent root review is recorded separately.
No full general arbitrary-ring TypeLoc theorem, new RecTExists proof, Lean replay, global automorphy or RH/GRH completion is asserted.
